problem:
A body of mass $1.5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)={t}^{4}-{t}^{3}$ meters.
Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-{t}^{3}) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}) \\  & =12{t}^{2}-6t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =1.5\cdot (12{t}^{2}-6t) \\  & =18{t}^{2}-9t.\end{aligned}
$$
